title: Graphite Stage — Hardware Keynote Hero
description: A device-centered keynote hero that floats a product render above a soft graphite gradient floor, with a single mono-sans name line and a pill-shaped availability chip — closer to a DJI product page than a PowerPoint slide.
philosophy: This template believes the product is the only speaker that matters. It rejects background texture, secondary copy blocks, and decorative gradients that compete with the hero render. It exists for hardware brands with enough confidence to let one line of type and a release date carry the entire slide — the kind of restraint that reads as authority in a darkened conference room or a livestream thumbnail.
goodFor: Keynote opening frames where the device IS the argument
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly earnings or financial reviews
Service or SaaS pitches with no physical hero asset
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a darkened stage the instant before a reveal — vast negative space holding one glowing object. The product render commands total authority, lit from above with a faint soft shadow spilling onto the gradient floor below. Mood is restrained confidence bordering on silence: one name, one release marker, nothing competing. Avoid texture, secondary copy blocks, or decorative gradients that share visual weight with the hero; the drama lives entirely in the object and the surrounding dark.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas with a single centered vertical axis — product render fills the upper two-thirds of the stage, floating above a soft radial gradient floor that dissolves into the background at the bottom edge. Product name sits centered below the render with generous vertical separation, followed immediately by the pill-shaped availability chip on the same axis. No header band, no footer rule, no page number; the sole structural logic is the three-element center stack: render, name, chip.

examples.promptCore: A hardware spec-reveal slide that carries the same quiet authority as a premium materials teardown page — engineering honesty, zero ornament. The left half is grounded by a tight macro crop of the product's physical surface, edge, or port detail, making the object feel tactile and real. The right column reads like a restrained data sheet: stacked, rule-separated entries with a single pill chip labeling the category. Avoid any gradient that draws attention to itself, decorative iconography, or copy volume that dilutes the single-subject confidence the template demands.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; a bleed-left cropped product surface or edge-detail image occupies cols 1–5, while cols 6–12 hold a vertically stacked spec block anchored by a pill-shaped category chip at top. Horizontal rule lines between spec entries serve as the sole hierarchy mechanism — no nested containers or background cards. Page number sits bottom-right outside the live area; outer top and bottom margins breathe at roughly 6–7% to preserve the stage-like negative space that defines the template's character.
